text:
Katie Zacharia, the former White House press secretary hired and fired in the same week, is under investigation by the state bar of California for claiming to be a lawyer despite never passing the bar exam.
Earlier this month, the state bar of California informed Campaign for Accountability, a non-profit watchdog group, that it had assigned an investigator and legal adviser to investigate Zacharia after the organization filed a complaint.
Before her short stint as Donald Trump’s press secretary, Zacharia repeatedly represented herself as a lawyer on cable news programs and had claimed on her LinkedIn profile that she served as the general counsel for a non-profit organization in California.
Trump also identified Zacharia as an “attorney” when announcing her appointment.
While Zacharia received a law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, she never passed the bar exam in California or any other US state.
“Zacharia may have thought she was just playing a lawyer on TV, but by repeatedly holding herself out as an attorney on news programs, she was pretending to have authority she lacks,” Michelle Kuppersmith, the director of the Campaign for Accountability, said in a statement.
“We’re pleased the California Bar is taking this matter seriously and investigating,” Kuppersmith added.
A spokesperson for Zacharia said in a statement to the Guardian: “These are baseless allegations. This complaint is politically motivated and a clear waste of the State Bar’s time and resources. We are confident it will be dismissed with no finding of wrongdoing.”
Zacharia previously defended describing herself as a “lawyer”, claiming there was a difference between a “lawyer” and an “attorney”, a title reserved for those licensed to practice law. In her email to the Guardian, Zacharia linked to an American Bar Association Journal article distinguishing the two terms.
The Guardian has asked the state bar of California for comment.
The Campaign for Accountability had submitted a complaint to the state bar of California in mid-October.
“In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime. The State Bar should investigate whether Ms. Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials and hold her accountable if she has,” the non-profit watchdog organization wrote in their complaint.
Zacharia became the shortest-serving White House press secretary when she replaced Karoline Leavitt in mid-October for just five days. From the start, she struggled to fit into the role, stumbling over words during her first press briefing and only taking questions from predominantly conservative media outlets.
digest_he:
קייטי זכריה, שכיהנה כדוברת הבית הלבן למשך חמישה ימים בלבד באוקטובר האחרון, נמצאת תחת חקירה של לשכת עורכי הדין בקליפורניה. החקירה החלה בעקבות תלונה שהגישה קבוצת הפיקוח הציבורית Campaign for Accountability, הטוענת כי זכריה הציגה את עצמה פעמים רבות כעורכת דין בתוכניות טלוויזיה וברשתות חברתיות, אף על פי מעולם לא עברה את בחינות הלשכה בקליפורניה או בכל מדינה אחרת בארצות הברית, על אף שהשלימה לימודי משפטים באוניברסיטת פפרדין ב-2011.

מטעם זכריה נמסר בתגובה כי מדובר בטענות חסרות בסיס ובתלונה בעלת מניעים פוליטיים שנועדה לבזבז את משאבי לשכת עורכי הדין, והם הביעו ביטחון שהתיק ייסגר ללא ממצאים על התנהגות פסולה. זכריה עצמה טענה בעבר כי יש הבדל בין התואר lawyer לבין attorney המורשה לעסוק בפועל בעריכת דין. הלשכה טרם הגיבה רשמית לפניות כלי התקשורת בנושא.
